Epic to track OPCT release activities.

Goals:

* Link all Epics, tasks or OCPBUGS that must be included and wait by in this Epic
* Link/Block any Partner Review Epic which is waiting for that release
* Review [Quay.io|http://Quay.io] repository for all images if needs to update dependencies to fix issues from security scanner
** Open PR for each update
* Merge all PRs that needs to be included in the release (make sure related tasks/Epics are attached)
* Test:
** Test locally and update comments - can be child tasks
* Release:
** Note: best practice create a Release Candidate (RC) before regular release to validate on CI
** Create Tag and Release Plugin Repository
** Create Tag and Release OPCT Repository
*** update types.go with new plugins image
* Update CI configuration with new version
** Update opct image version
** Additional task: Review if there is OCP versions to be updated. Ex new jobs for 5.1, move 5.0 to weekly when it’s stable version (eg. has EC or RC versions)
* Validate CI jobs with new version
** validate first RC, then GA if required/complex changes
* Promote RC to GA
* Edit (manually) the Github release to {{latest}}: go to [opct project releases|https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/releases] > choose the release to promote  > *Release label*: {{Latest}}
* Notify the Slack channel with the new release
* Close

items.fromString:
*Goal:*
Fix the bug [OCPBUGS-77783|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-77783] and ensure that the kubernetes and openshift conformance suites executed by OPCT produce a consistent and correct test list across all OCP versions supported to VCSP validations.

*Why:*
As described in [OCPBUGS-77783|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-77783], starting with OCP 4.20 the conformance suites {{kubernetes/conformance}} and {{openshift/conformance-validated}} executed by OPCT are inconsistent with historical behavior (4.18/4.19) and with the {{e2e-external}} [workflows|https://prow.ci.openshift.org/?job=*openshift-release-*e2e-external*].

This behavior blocks provider VCSP validation for OCP 4.20+ releases and impacts partners validating offerings in the "Full Support" phase.

*Acceptance criteria:*

* Bug fixed in the mainstream branch (OPCT templates and openshift-tests-plugin as needed)
** Fix verified in CI jobs covering all impacted OCP workflows
** Identify which OCP versions Z-stream are impacted and document in the OPCT supported matrix: [https://redhat-openshift-ecosystem.github.io/opct/guides/cluster-validation/#openshift-and-opct-versions|https://redhat-openshift-ecosystem.github.io/opct/guides/cluster-validation/#openshift-and-opct-versions]
* Validate the fixed workflow end-to-end for each supported OCP minor from 4.20 onward (4.20, 4.21, 4.22, and newer as they become supported)
** {{10-openshift-kube-conformance}} and {{20-openshift-conformance-validated}} test list counts are stable and within expected ranges (documented)
* Documentation updated and partners/stakeholders informed when the fix is available

As described in [OCPBUGS-77783|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-77783], starting with OCP 4.21 the conformance suites {{openshift/conformance-validated}} executed by OPCT are inconsistent with historical behavior (4.18/4.19) and with the {{e2e-external}} [workflows|https://prow.ci.openshift.org/?job=*openshift-release-*e2e-external*].

This behavior blocks provider VCSP validation for OCP 4.21+ releases and impacts partners validating offerings in the "Full Support" phase.

*Acceptance criteria:*

* Bug fixed in the mainstream branch (OPCT templates and openshift-tests-plugin as needed)
** Fix verified in CI jobs covering all impacted OCP workflows
** Identify which OCP versions Z-stream are impacted and document in the OPCT supported matrix: [https://redhat-openshift-ecosystem.github.io/opct/guides/cluster-validation/#openshift-and-opct-versions|https://redhat-openshift-ecosystem.github.io/opct/guides/cluster-validation/#openshift-and-opct-versions]
* Validate the fixed workflow end-to-end for each supported OCP minor from 4.21 onward (4.21 and newer as they become supported)
**  {{20-openshift-conformance-validated}} test list counts are stable and within expected ranges (documented)
* Documentation updated and partners/stakeholders informed when the fix is available

Validate OPCT conformance workflow results on OCP 4.22 after fix fir [+OCPBUGS-77783+|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-77783]

*Goal*

Confirm the OCPBUGS-77783 fix behaves correctly on OCP 4.22 and that OPCT

conformance workflows produce stable, expected test counts.

*Scope*

* Validate via CI jobs in `openshift/release`, e.g.: `periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-4.22-opct-external-aws-ccm`
* Any relevant 4.21 platform-external jobs (e.g. vsphere).
* Optionally run OPCT manually against a 4.22 cluster using the fixed stack.
* For each run, evaluate if each step are under expected range:
** `10-openshift-kube-conformance` test count matches the range expected by kubernetes conformance suite (parallel),
** `20-openshift-conformance-validated` test count matches the e2e workflow, ex: [periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-4.22-e2e-external-aws|https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results/logs/periodic-ci-openshift-release-main-nightly-4.22-e2e-external-aws/2048190819759820800]
* Pass/fail, links to logs.

*Acceptance criteria*

* The reference of at least one successful 4.22 CI run with the fixed bug
* Test counts for both suites are stable and within agreed ranges for 4.21.
* Comparison vs: historical 4.18/4.19 behavior, 4.22 `e2e-external` suites, [https://prow.ci.openshift.org/?job=*openshift-release-*e2e-external*|https://prow.ci.openshift.org/?job=*openshift-release-*e2e-external*], is documented, and any differences are explained.

Communicate OCPBUGS-77783 resolution and guidance to VCSP/CCSP partners and internal teams

**Goal**

Ensure VCSP/CCSP partners and internal stakeholders understand the resolution of

OCPBUGS-77783 and how to proceed with OCP 4.20+ validations using OPCT.

**Scope**

* Draft a concise communication covering:

* What OCPBUGS-77783 was and its impact on conformance test counts.

* Fixed versions:

* OCP,

* OPCT,

* openshift-tests-plugin.

* Expected test-count behavior on 4.20+ after the fix.

* Required/Recommended partner actions (e.g. re-run with fixed stack).

* Links to:

* OCPBUGS-77783,

* Epic OPCT-383,

* Updated OPCT docs (version skew + conformance).

* Example CI jobs.

* Share via:

* Internal channels (e.g. SPLAT / Ecosystem / VCSP Slack),

* VCSP/CCSP program communication for affected partners.

* Capture feedback and open follow-ups as necessary.

**Acceptance criteria**

* At least one internal message and, if applicable, partner-facing message is

  linked to this issue.

* Key stakeholders (Cert-Ops, PTAMs, VCSP program, SPLAT, etc.) acknowledge the

  guidance.

* Any follow-up work requested is either handled here or tracked as new issues

  linked to OPCT-383.

*** Total tests for `20-openshift-conformance-validated`,
** Pass/fail counts,
* Links to job logs.

*Acceptance criteria*

* At least one successful 4.20 CI run using the fix proposal.

*Goal:*
Fix the bug [OCPBUGS-77783|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-77783] and ensure that the kubernetes and openshift conformance suites executed by OPCT produce a consistent and correct test list across all OCP versions supported to VCSP validations.

*Why:*
As described in [OCPBUGS-77783|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-77783], starting with OCP 4.20 the conformance suites {{kubernetes/conformance}} and {{openshift/conformance-validated}} executed by OPCT are inconsistent with historical behavior (4.18/4.19) and with the {{e2e-external}} [workflows|https://prow.ci.openshift.org/?job=*openshift-release-*e2e-external*].

This behavior blocks provider VCSP validation for OCP 4.20+ releases and impacts partners validating offerings in the "Full Support" phase.

*Acceptance criteria:*

* Bug fixed in the mainstream branch (OPCT templates and openshift-tests-plugin as needed)
** Fix verified in CI jobs covering all impacted OCP workflows
** Identify which OCP versions Z-stream are impacted and document in the OPCT supported matrix: [https://redhat-openshift-ecosystem.github.io/opct/guides/cluster-validation/#openshift-and-opct-versions|https://redhat-openshift-ecosystem.github.io/opct/guides/cluster-validation/#openshift-and-opct-versions]
* Validate the fixed workflow end-to-end for each supported OCP minor from 4.20 onward (4.20, 4.21, 4.22, and newer as they become supported)
** {{10-openshift-kube-conformance}} and {{20-openshift-conformance-validated}} test list counts are stable and within expected ranges (documented)
* Documentation updated and partners/stakeholders informed when the fix is available

items.fromString:
+*Goal:*+

Fix the bug OCPBUGS-78617 and provide back port to previous OCP versions impacted by this bug, and supported by VCSP

*Why:*

As described in the bug, OPCT environment is crashing caused by a node restart performed from an e2e test executed in one of the conformance test triggered by the workflow, consequently no partners applying to VCSP program can validate their environment

*Acceptance criteria:*

* Bug fixed in the mainstream branch
** Fix verified in CI job in the  OCP branch targeting the mainstream branch
** Identify which OCP version the bug has been added to document when partner is facing the issue
* Back port to OCP 4.18
items.toString:
+*Goal:*+

Fix the bug OCPBUGS-78617 and provide backports to previous OCP versions impacted by this bug, and supported by VCSP

*Why:*

As described in the bug, OPCT environment is crashing due to a node restart performed from an e2e test executed in one of the conformance test triggered by the workflow, consequently, no partners applying to VCSP program can validate their environment

*Acceptance criteria:*

* Bug fixed in the mainstream branch
** Fix verified in CI job in the OCP branch targeting the mainstream branch
** Identify which OCP version the bug has been added, so that we can document impacted OCP versions when partner going to face the issue. We’ll have a gap between unsupported OCP releases, it must be correctly documented in the version skew [https://redhat-openshift-ecosystem.github.io/opct/guides/cluster-validation/#openshift-and-opct-versions|https://redhat-openshift-ecosystem.github.io/opct/guides/cluster-validation/#openshift-and-opct-versions|smart-link] 
* Backport to OCP 4.18

*User Story:*
As an OpenShift Engineer I want to fix the OPCT conformance workflow for platform external to set 'provider' as external to the openshift-tests so tests configured to skip in that platform will be ignored in the execution, preventing scheduling known failures cases.

*Description:*
< Record any background information >

The openshift-tests-plugin must:
 * detect the running cluster is platform type External. See case eval: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/provider-certification-plugins/blob/main/openshift-tests-plugin/plugin/platform.sh#L127] 
 * implement the function to set the flag --provider to the openshift tests. See example for AWS: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/provider-certification-plugins/blob/main/openshift-tests-plugin/plugin/platform.sh#L66-L87]
 * Create an image (then release) of OPCT plugin
 * Install OCP cluster with platform type External
 * Run plugin image override in CLI
 * Check the logs of conformance step logs if the openshift-tests sets the provider=external
 * check if the sample test is skipped, example 

*Acceptance Criteria:*
< Record how we'll know we're done >

*Other Information:*
< Record anything else that may be helpful to someone else picking up the card >

*User Story:*
 * As an OpenShift Engineer I want create a minimum "user documentation" template required to a partner when applying to VCSP ticket, so partners have a clear path of minimum expected information to have in the provider-specific installation documentation requested in the Process Overview workflow[1].

[1] [https://redhat-openshift-ecosystem.github.io/opct/guides/cluster-validation/#process-overview] 

Existing documents/guides:
 * Installation Review: [https://redhat-openshift-ecosystem.github.io/opct/guides/cluster-validation/installation-review/]|
 * Installation Checklist: [https://redhat-openshift-ecosystem.github.io/opct/guides/cluster-validation/installation-checklist/]
 * Past partners documentation/references>
 ** [G42Cloud|https://drive.google.com/file/d/13S--Sym6YlvroPbEKVQcpwJGYQ67TsUR/view]
 ** Oracle[ https://docs.oracle.com/pt-br/iaas/Content/openshift-on-oci/overview.htm|https://docs.oracle.com/pt-br/iaas/Content/openshift-on-oci/overview.htm]
 ** Other list from OPCT Entrypoint document: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xj-E8o2xffWa3G1MhHzJ_opYnNXMB_Kzliuj9TDBjzk/edit?tab=t.0]

 * Document must target the audience:
 ** VCSP Reviewers: must provide provider's information helping to understand the provider's nuances derivated from the OCP agnostic installation documentation.

 * Document reviewed by stakeholders (PM, PTAM, CertOps, Eng)
 * Public document available to partners
 ** Where (git, gdocs, etc)? Who will maintain?

Story:
 * As a Engineer, I would like to ensure the matrix of supported platform type is valid, so partners can quickly detect prior VCSP ticket that their result are valid or not
 * As a Partner applying to VCSP, I want to know if my installation is valid by VCSP, so that I can resolve it prior applying a ticket to validation OCP on VCSP.

 

Goal:
 * Create a Check/SLO checking if the platform type vs install method matrix is valid
 * Supported platform type and install method:
 ** openshift-install with platform type External
 ** Assisted Installer with platform type None (User-managed networking mode)
 ** Agent-Based Installer with platform type External (?)
 *** Is there a special config map for ABI which does not exists in AI?
 * How to validate the install-method?: Check the following configuration

{code:java}
$ omc get cm openshift-install-manifests -n openshift-config -o json | jq .data.invoker
"assisted-installer"

$ omc get cm openshift-install-manifests -n openshift-config -o json | jq .data.invoker
"user" {code}

Story:
 * As a Engineer, I would like to ensure the matrix of supported platform type is valid, so partners can quickly detect prior VCSP ticket that their result are valid or not
 * As a Partner applying to VCSP, I want to know if my installation is valid by VCSP, so that I can resolve it prior applying a ticket to validation OCP on VCSP.

 

Goal:
 * Create a Check/SLO checking if the platform type vs install method matrix is valid
 * Supported platform type and install method:
 ** openshift-install with platform type External
 ** Assisted Installer with platform type None (User-managed networking mode)
 ** Agent-Based Installer with platform type External (?)
 *** Is there a special config map for ABI which does not exists in AI?
 * How to validate the install-method?: Check the following configuration

{code:java}
# cluster installed with openshift-install
$ omc get cm openshift-install-manifests -n openshift-config -o json | jq .data.invoker
"user" 

# cluster installed with assisted-installer
$ omc get cm openshift-install-manifests -n openshift-config -o json | jq .data.invoker
"assisted-installer"

# cluster installed with agent-based installer
$ oc  get cm openshift-install-manifests -n openshift-config -o json | jq .data.invoker
"agent-installer"{code}
 

*References:*
 * Slack thread discussing the scope:
 ** [https://redhat-internal.slack.com/archives/C03UZKBRHT5/p1740576413182999]
 ** ABI tests: [https://redhat-internal.slack.com/archives/C03UZKBRHT5/p1741683286674639?thread_ts=1740576413.182999&cid=C03UZKBRHT5]
 * None deprecation document: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1emH4dD75Gne47eW0prjuSjM0D_IkHP1UFRekFIG5SDE/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.66y4kqbj468a]

Story{*}:{*}
 * As a OpenShift engineer I would like to create a mechanism to prevent e2e tests failing when randomly trying to schedule in the OPCT dedicated node, preventing false-positive in the final conformance results so that we can improve the visibility and decrease the maintenance friction in the OPCT architecture to run conformance workflow in-cluster
 * As Partner I would like to get more visibility of tests failing exclusively for my test environment, so that I can self-review, and isolate failures easily.
 * As Cert-Ops Engineer I would like to review a partner result quickly with non-OPCT environmental failures causing false-positives, so that we can provide a feedback quickly to the partner

*Goal:*
 * Create a Controller to watch pods failed to schedule caused by OPCT dedicated node (a worker node with NoSchedule taints), mutate those adding toleration allowing to schedule in the dedicated node

 

_Why:_
 * Dedicated node has been created to prevent disruptions in the test environment by the scheduler forcing to evict the test services (Sonobuoy aggregator, workflow jobs, etc). 

 

Disclaimer: We can't deliver, at least in the current architecture, a stable solution without a dedicated node, or need to change the architecture to run the test environment off-cluster (envtest?). But it will require more time to research, and stable connectivity between client and cluster (which sometimes is a challenge - it was in the early partner applications).

 

*Acceptance Criteria:*
 * Controller created under the OPCT project repo
 * The controller entry point command must be 'opct adm e2e-dedicated controller' (or anything under 'opct adm e2e-dedicated')
 * The version must be validated with e2e tests (currently there is not periodic, you can push your image and run a rehearsal job in the release repo - see also OPCT-348 )
 * The PR in OPCT project must be merged

 

*References:*
 * Spike: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/pull/160/files]
 * Issues related (false-positive failed tests) attached to the epic OPCT-332

 * Dedicated node has been created to prevent disruptions in the test environment by the scheduler forcing to evict the test services (Sonobuoy aggregator, workflow jobs, etc). 

 

Disclaimer: We can't deliver, at least in the current architecture, a stable solution without a dedicated node, or need to change the architecture to run the test environment off-cluster (envtest?). But it will require more time to research, and stable connectivity between client and cluster (which sometimes is a challenge - it was in the early partner applications).

 

*Acceptance Criteria:*
 * Controller created under the OPCT project repo
 * The controller entry point command must be 'opct adm e2e-dedicated controller' (or anything under 'opct adm e2e-dedicated')
 * The version must be validated with e2e tests (currently there is not periodic, you can push your image and run a rehearsal job in the release repo - see also OPCT-348 )
 * The PR in OPCT project must be merged

 

*References:*
 * Spike: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/pull/160/files]
 * Issues related (false-positive failed tests) attached to the epic OPCT-332

*User Story:*
As an OpenShift Engineer I want to review, and fix, the upgrade workflow which is failing on CI starting on 4.18 due (new?) restrictions while creating the "opct" MachineConfigPool - required by OPCT upgrade workflow for the dedicated node so that partners can validate upgrade workflow in 4.18->4.19. 4.17 (opct-main-4.17-platform-none-vsphere-upgrade) upgrade is working as expected..

*Description:*

{code:java}
time="2025-03-09T05:50:49Z" level=info msg="Setting up node ci-op-ril1y0yi-0e310-nw2jb-compute-1..."

The machineconfigpools "opct" is invalid: : ValidatingAdmissionPolicy 'custom-machine-config-pool-selector' with binding 'custom-machine-config-pool-selector-binding' denied request: All custom MachineConfigPools must inherit from the worker pool and must have a machineConfigSelector that matches for a 'machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: worker' label

error: failed to execute wrapped command: exit status 1 
INFO[2025-03-09T05:50:50Z] Step platform-none-vsphere-upgrade-opct-pre-dedicated failed after 8s. 
INFO[2025-03-09T05:50:50Z] Step phase pre failed after 47m54s.    {code}
 

 

 

*Acceptance Criteria:*

items.fromString:
*User Story:*
As an Engineer I want to enhance the OPCT retrieve cleaner to remove the unused objects `packages.operators.coreos.com_v1_packagemanifests.json` collected by namespace so the final file size can be reduced to 1/3 from the original file (sample 4.19: 170MiB->58MiB), saving CI storage (cloud bills), partner support storage (Partner Connect system), and faster processing time.

*Description:*

Currently Sonobuoy, backed by OPCT, collects all kubernetes objects, cluster and namespace's scope, when the jobs have been finished, putting all together in the final archive, resulting in a file with size around 170 MiB (4.19 sample). The compressor does not apply deduplication, and we don't want to implement it in the Sonobuoy.

Recently the opct created a hook to patch the archive file when downloading the archive from the cluster to the local disk (client-side) to prevent leaking security credentials eventually exposed to non-secret objects in the cluster (such as pull-secret) - this command can be accessed through 'opct adm cleaner --input <unclear file> --output <cleaned file>' to apply the cleaner in old archives.

This patch can be enhanced to clean undesired/duplicated files too. Here is the path of cleaner:
 * Acting when retrieving/downloading the results: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/pkg/retrieve/retrieve.go#L118-L122] 
 * Cleaner package/rules: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/internal/cleaner/cleaner.go] 
 * Adm command to access the cleaner: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/pkg/cmd/adm/cleaner.go] 

 

*Acceptance Criteria:*
 * Cleaner implemented in CLI, preventing the final archive to keep duplicated/unsused files `packages.operators.coreos.com_v1_packagemanifests.json`
 * Unit tests implemented/updated
 * Tests the results by comparing the cleaner in a rehearsal CI job
 * PR merged in the OPCT CLI

items.toString:
*User Story:*
As an Engineer I want to enhance the OPCT retrieve cleaner to remove the unused objects `packages.operators.coreos.com_v1_packagemanifests.json` collected by namespace so the final file size can be reduced to 1/3 from the original file (sample 4.19: 170MiB->58MiB), saving CI storage (cloud bills), partner support storage (Partner Connect system), and faster processing time.

*Description:*

Currently Sonobuoy, backed by OPCT, collects all kubernetes objects, cluster and namespace's scope, when the jobs have been finished, putting all together in the final archive, resulting in a file with size around 170 MiB (4.19 sample). The compressor does not apply deduplication, and we don't want to implement it in the Sonobuoy.

Recently the opct created a hook to patch the archive file when downloading the archive from the cluster to the local disk (client-side) to prevent leaking security credentials eventually exposed to non-secret objects in the cluster (such as pull-secret) - this command can be accessed through 'opct adm cleaner --input <unclear file> --output <cleaned file>' to apply the cleaner in old archives.

This patch can be enhanced to clean undesired/duplicated files too. Here is the path of cleaner:
 * Acting when retrieving/downloading the results: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/pkg/retrieve/retrieve.go#L118-L122] 
 * Cleaner package/rules: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/internal/cleaner/cleaner.go] 
 * Adm command to access the cleaner: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/pkg/cmd/adm/cleaner.go] 

 

*Acceptance Criteria:*
 * Cleaner implemented in CLI, preventing the final archive to keep duplicated/unused files `packages.operators.coreos.com_v1_packagemanifests.json`
 * Unit tests implemented/updated (see the child cards)
 * Tests the results by comparing the cleaner in a rehearsal CI job
 * PR merged in the OPCT CLI

items.fromString:
*User Story:*
As an Engineer I want to enhance the OPCT retrieve cleaner to remove the duplicated objects `packages.operators.coreos.com_v1_packagemanifests.json` collected by namespace so the final file size can be reduced to 1/3 from the original file (sample 4.19: 170MiB->58MiB), saving CI storage (cloud bills), partner support storage (Partner Connect system), and faster processing time.

*Description:*

Currently Sonobuoy, backed by OPCT, collects all kubernetes objects, cluster and namespace's scope, when the jobs have been finished, putting all together in the final archive, resulting in a file with size around 170 MiB (4.19 sample). The compressor does not apply deduplication, and we don't want to implement it in the Sonobuoy.

Recently the opct created a hook to patch the archive file when downloading the archive from the cluster to the local disk (client-side) to prevent leaking security credentials eventually exposed to non-secret objects in the cluster (such as pull-secret) - this command can be accessed through 'opct adm cleaner --input <unclear file> --output <cleaned file>' to apply the cleaner in old archives.

This patch can be enhanced to clean undesired/duplicated files too. Here is the path of cleaner:
 * Acting when retrieving/downloading the results: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/pkg/retrieve/retrieve.go#L118-L122] 
 * Cleaner package/rules: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/internal/cleaner/cleaner.go] 
 * Adm command to access the cleaner: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/pkg/cmd/adm/cleaner.go] 

 

*Acceptance Criteria:*
 * Cleaner implemented in CLI, preventing the final archive to keep duplicated/unsused files `packages.operators.coreos.com_v1_packagemanifests.json`
 * Unit tests implemented/updated
 * Tests the results by comparing the cleaner in a rehearsal CI job
 * PR merged in the OPCT CLI

items.toString:
*User Story:*
As an Engineer I want to enhance the OPCT retrieve cleaner to remove the unused objects `packages.operators.coreos.com_v1_packagemanifests.json` collected by namespace so the final file size can be reduced to 1/3 from the original file (sample 4.19: 170MiB->58MiB), saving CI storage (cloud bills), partner support storage (Partner Connect system), and faster processing time.

*Description:*

Currently Sonobuoy, backed by OPCT, collects all kubernetes objects, cluster and namespace's scope, when the jobs have been finished, putting all together in the final archive, resulting in a file with size around 170 MiB (4.19 sample). The compressor does not apply deduplication, and we don't want to implement it in the Sonobuoy.

Recently the opct created a hook to patch the archive file when downloading the archive from the cluster to the local disk (client-side) to prevent leaking security credentials eventually exposed to non-secret objects in the cluster (such as pull-secret) - this command can be accessed through 'opct adm cleaner --input <unclear file> --output <cleaned file>' to apply the cleaner in old archives.

This patch can be enhanced to clean undesired/duplicated files too. Here is the path of cleaner:
 * Acting when retrieving/downloading the results: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/pkg/retrieve/retrieve.go#L118-L122] 
 * Cleaner package/rules: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/internal/cleaner/cleaner.go] 
 * Adm command to access the cleaner: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/pkg/cmd/adm/cleaner.go] 

 

*Acceptance Criteria:*
 * Cleaner implemented in CLI, preventing the final archive to keep duplicated/unsused files `packages.operators.coreos.com_v1_packagemanifests.json`
 * Unit tests implemented/updated
 * Tests the results by comparing the cleaner in a rehearsal CI job
 * PR merged in the OPCT CLI

items.fromString:
*User Story:*
As an Engineer I want to enhance the OPCT retrieve cleaner to remove the duplicated objects `packages.operators.coreos.com_v1_packagemanifests.json` collected by namespace so the final file size can be reduced to 1/3 from the original file (sample 4.19: 170MiB->58MiB), saving CI storage (cloud bills), partner support storage (Partner Connect system), and faster processing time.

*Description:*

Currently Sonobuoy, backed by OPCT, collects all kubernetes objects, cluster and namespace's scope, when the jobs have been finished, putting all together in the final archive, resulting in a file with size around 170 MiB (4.19 sample). The compressor does not apply deduplication, and we don't want to implement it in the Sonobuoy.

Recently the opct created a hook to patch the archive file when downloading the archive from the cluster to the local disk (client-side) to prevent leaking security credentials eventually exposed to non-secret objects in the cluster (such as pull-secret) - this command can be accessed through 'opct adm cleaner --input <unclear file> --output <cleaned file>' to apply the cleaner in old archives.

This patch can be enhanced to clean undesired/duplicated files too. Here is the path of cleaner:
 * Acting when retrieving/downloading the results: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/pkg/retrieve/retrieve.go#L118-L122] 
 * Cleaner package/rules: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/internal/cleaner/cleaner.go] 
 * Adm command to access the cleaner: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/pkg/cmd/adm/cleaner.go] 

 

*Acceptance Criteria:*
 * Cleaner implemented in CLI, preventing the final archive to keep duplicated/unsused files `packages.operators.coreos.com_v1_packagemanifests.json`
 * Unit tests implemented/updated
 * Tests the results by comparing the cleaner in a rehearsal CI job
 * PR merged in the OPCT CLI

 

*Other Information:*

items.toString:
*User Story:*
As an Engineer I want to enhance the OPCT retrieve cleaner to remove the duplicated objects `packages.operators.coreos.com_v1_packagemanifests.json` collected by namespace so the final file size can be reduced to 1/3 from the original file (sample 4.19: 170MiB->58MiB), saving CI storage (cloud bills), partner support storage (Partner Connect system), and faster processing time.

*Description:*

Currently Sonobuoy, backed by OPCT, collects all kubernetes objects, cluster and namespace's scope, when the jobs have been finished, putting all together in the final archive, resulting in a file with size around 170 MiB (4.19 sample). The compressor does not apply deduplication, and we don't want to implement it in the Sonobuoy.

Recently the opct created a hook to patch the archive file when downloading the archive from the cluster to the local disk (client-side) to prevent leaking security credentials eventually exposed to non-secret objects in the cluster (such as pull-secret) - this command can be accessed through 'opct adm cleaner --input <unclear file> --output <cleaned file>' to apply the cleaner in old archives.

This patch can be enhanced to clean undesired/duplicated files too. Here is the path of cleaner:
 * Acting when retrieving/downloading the results: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/pkg/retrieve/retrieve.go#L118-L122] 
 * Cleaner package/rules: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/internal/cleaner/cleaner.go] 
 * Adm command to access the cleaner: [https://github.com/redhat-openshift-ecosystem/opct/blob/main/pkg/cmd/adm/cleaner.go] 

 

*Acceptance Criteria:*
 * Cleaner implemented in CLI, preventing the final archive to keep duplicated/unsused files `packages.operators.coreos.com_v1_packagemanifests.json`
 * Unit tests implemented/updated
 * Tests the results by comparing the cleaner in a rehearsal CI job
 * PR merged in the OPCT CLI

 

*Other Information:*
< Record anything else that may be helpful to someone else picking up the card >

{*}Goal{*}:
 * Allow incoming workloads to be scheduled in the dedicated node, which has NoSchedule taint, when e2e suite is running, preventing false-positive issues, like OCPBUGS-31407 

*Suggested solution:*
 * 1/ Create a mutation webhook to patch any e2e workload to the dedicated node to have the required toleration
 * 2/ Create a mechanism to make the pods failing to schedule caused by 'dedicated node' (tainted worker node required by OPCT architecture) to not fail in the final test results, having minimum impact in the conformance test execution: create a controller watching all failed pods, mutating it to allow scheduling in the tainted node by applying the required tolerations to the pod spec.

*Why:*
 * Almost every execution of OPCT there are false-positive failures due tests trying to schedule workloads in the dedicated node and getting failure
 * This is caused by OPCT architecture using dedicated node preventing running the controller (aggregator server) in client side to prevent issues with client connectivity with OCP cluster. So it would not be possible to add exceptions to OCP product for non-OCP utility (OPCT).
 * Change the OPCT environment would be more complicated due factor aforementioned.

Acceptance Criteria:

-

items.fromString:
* Evaluate the CI job results if the kube-burner feature is aggregating value to the final artifacts.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
 * Tested v0.6-alpha* release with kube-burner must no increase much time in the final job execution
 * Artifacts must not increase much (>5MiB) in size
 * The data collected have proofed the minimum value. Examples:
 ** standard kube-burner profiles is collecting similar metrics used when evaluating integrated providers of performance (non-scale)
 ** metrics isn't duplicated with existing metrics collector - priority for kube-burner metrics if we need to decide/prevent duplicated data collected
 ** we can provide a minimum guide of what to extract from the kube-burner results along side the metrics/target and expected values, such as:
 *** Control Plane: Node-density light: p99 podReady latency should be <=3s
 *** Control Plane: Node-density heavy: p99 podReady latency should be <=41s
 *** Control Plane: Node-density CNI: p99 podReady latency should be <=5s
 *** Cluster-density-v2:
 **** Pod ready latency: p99 pod ready latency of all members: <target value TBD in baseline topology>
 **** Etcd fsync latency: Avg 99th fsync latency of all members: <target value TBD in baseline topology>
 **** Etcd commit latency: Avg 99th commit of all members: <target value TBD in baseline topology>
 **** Etcd round trip latency: Avg P99 round trip of all members: <target value TBD in baseline topology>
 **** Read only API request P99 latency - resource scoped: Avg P99 latency : <target value TBD in baseline topology>
 **** Read only API request P99 latency - namespace scoped: Avg P99 latency : <target value TBD in baseline topology>
 **** Mutating API request P99 latency - namespace scoped: Avg P99 latency : <target value TBD in baseline topology>

Goals:
 * Review if the jobs is not taking long to execute
 * Review if the data collected from kube-burner is aggregating information to have an overview of baseline performance of kube-api, etcd, and other metrics collected by the standard kube-burner profiles used to ensure readiness in OCP releases
 * Review if the stable v0.6 will deliver kube-burner as opt-in or opt-out.
 ** If we'll opt-out by default, a flag must be added to enable it when running the workflow ('run' command)

Overall results from regular conformance workflow ran well in a management cluster installed in self-managed OCP on AWS. Key notes
 * The results are as expected. The Baseline API is not providing data as OPCT jobs for 4.19 is not feeding the API yet.
 * For regular OPCT workflow in OpenShift clusters:
 ** Kube conformance is passing
 ** OpenShift conformance are failing under the expected threshold non-GA OCP
 * For dedicated e2e in hypershift:
 ** I did a initial exploration, unfortunately my cluster has been pruned, but initial results were promised. The sub-task OPCT-318 will capture the results.

items.fromString:
The openshift-tests plugin tries to extract the credentials from the cluster in the e2e startup of openshift-tests utility, it supports only long-lived credentials.

If we want a fully integrated support in short-lived credentials, such as Manual mode (STS), a new approach need to be implemented to present the credentials to the step.

Environments affected:
- OCP clusters installed with short-lived credentials, such as OCP standalone with STS (AWS), or HCP Hosted Cluster on AWS

{code:java}
#> setting up cloud provider...
2025-02-04T19:50:20+00:00 | [platform] | platform:97>  [executor] discovering platform type...
2025-02-04T19:50:20+00:00 | [platform] | platform:101>  [executor] platform type=[aws]
2025-02-04T19:50:20+00:00 | [platform] | platform:48>  [executor] setting provider configuration for [aws]
Error from server (NotFound): secrets "aws-creds" not found
#> waiting for start command
{code}

items.fromString: OPCT [CLI] - Create a check/SLO to fail when the ciuster install is too old
items.toString: OPCT [CLI] - Create a check/SLO to fail when the cluster install is too old

items.fromString:
Goal:

As a Cert-Ops review, I would like to have an clear Check/SLO failing if the OpenShift installation is older than expected to prevent false-positive errors while reviewing the results, so I can have more confidence of checks and failed tests.

Description:

OPCT states in the documentation[1] that a fresh OpenShift installation, new cluster, must be created before running the conformance tests to prevent false positives.

This requirement comes from expected behaviors in OpenShift CI.

To check if the cluster is old, the following steps must be performed:
 * Extract the timestamp the cluster has been installed from cluster version
 * check when the OPCT server has finished
 * if the delta is older than 10 hours (double of expected OPCT execution time), the check/SLO must fail

Checking manully:
 - Time the cluster was installed

 
{code:java}
$ mkdir results
$ tar xfz opct_202408200704_96b783d7-2030-412a-853a-e16fd2d8644a.tar.gz -C results/

$ omc-devel use results/plugins/99-openshift-artifacts-collector/results/global/artifacts_must-gather.tar.xz 

$ omc get clusterversion version -o json | jq .status.history[].completionTime
"2024-08-15T05:59:53Z" {code}
 

 
 - Time the published conformance test has finished:

{code:java}
$ opct report --log-level=debug --skip-server --save-to report/ opct_202408200704_96b783d7-2030-412a-853a-e16fd2d8644a.tar.gz  

$ jq '.provider.runtime.serverLogs[] | select(.name=="server finished").time ' report/opct-report.json 
"2024-08-20T09:36:38Z"{code}
The delta above is more than 5 days, which trigger the failed check/SLO.

 * if the delta is older than 10 hours (double of expected OPCT execution time), the check/SLO must fail

Checking manully:

{code:java}
$ mkdir results
$ tar xfz opct_202408200704_96b783d7-2030-412a-853a-e16fd2d8644a.tar.gz -C results/

$ omc-devel use results/plugins/99-openshift-artifacts-collector/results/global/artifacts_must-gather.tar.xz

items.fromString: Metrics data is not correct collected in v0.5.0 release
items.toString:
Metrics data are not correct collected in v0.5.0 release.

 

Problem: metrics are not correctly collected during artifacts collector with must-gather-metrics exporter.

Reason: URI is not correctly encoded when constructing the URL query to Prometheus, then the request is rejected by server.

Steps to reproduce:
- run standalone metrics collector: `oc adm must-gather --image=quay.io/opct/must-gather-monitoring:v0.5.0`
- check the errors in: `must-gather.local.*/*/monitoring/prometheus/metrics/*.stderr`
